safety_lead_time.comparison_action: DECREASE from SAP 2.5 days to 1.70 days

narrative: Demand for PL1__MC0A352A is near-continuous (98.5% non-zero days) at ~3,942 units/day with a moderate CV of 0.30, classified as Variable/Right-skewed. Lead times are highly volatile (CV=0.665, range 0.63–5.26 days), and this variability dominates 87.5% of the safety stock requirement. The current SAP safety stock of 90 units is critically insufficient for the 95% service level target; 6,720 units are required. A continuous-review (r,Q) policy with EOQ lot sizing reduces orders from 628 to 82 per year, cutting total annual inventory cost by 59.9% while simultaneously meeting the service level target.
warnings: Current SAP safety stock (90) covers only 1.3% of statistically required buffer (6,720) — service level is at significant risk under current policy.

research_insights.selected_model: Continuous-review (r,Q) policy with EOQ lot sizing
research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is near-continuous with 98.5% non-zero days and moderate CV, making a continuous-review (r,Q) policy appropriate. EOQ lot sizing balances ordering and holding costs given the low unit cost and high annual volume (~985,425 units/year). The volatile lead time (CV=0.665) necessitates a statistically derived safety stock rather than SAP's fixed 90-unit buffer.
research_insights.boundary_risk: No capacity boundary risk — optimized policy (SS=6,720 + OQ=11,983 = 18,703 units) utilizes only 50.6% of available storage (36,932 units). MOQ of 1,568 is non-binding as EOQ (11,983) exceeds it comfortably.
